title: Tiered sampled retention and attested evidence exports for prompts, responses, logs, and metric rollups
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Problem statement: Customers need expressive retention controls that (1) reduce storage cost and privacy exposure for low-risk traffic by sampling, (2) retain high-fidelity data for high-risk routes/tenants, and (3) produce cryptographically verifiable evidence bundles for audits and regulators. Current retention features support per-route TTLs and simple archival; they do not provide: tiered hot/cold/archive policies, deterministic sampling semantics tied to tenant/route/model variants, or an attestable evidence export format with signed manifests and residency constraints.

Goal: Design and deliver a tiered retention model that supports sampled retention for prompts/responses/request logs and separate retention windows for metric rollups. Provide an automated evidence export pipeline that produces signed, residency-aware bundles (including manifests, checksums, export logs, and KMS-wrapped encryption keys) and a retention-preview report that shows projected storage and compliance footprints before changes are applied.

Non-goals: Not implementing an entire archival retrieval UI in this iteration; not changing existing billing models.

Why this matters: Many customers operate under data minimization or regulator-driven sampling requirements (e.g., keeping 1% of requests for 5 years for audit while deleting the rest sooner). Without deterministic sampling and provable export metadata customers cannot attest to regulators. This feature also unlocks cost reductions for customers and Redwood by enabling predictable cold storage usage and targeted evidence exports.
acceptance_criteria: Admin UI exposes retention tiers: hot (immediate), warm (sampled), cold (archive) and a metric-rollup retention slider per tenant/route.
Sampling rules support deterministic hashing (seeded by tenant id + route id) with configurable sample rate and route overrides.
Evidence export job produces a tar.gz bundle per-request-window that includes: JSON manifest, checksums, signed manifest (ECDSA), KMS-encrypted symmetric key, and residency metadata.
Export bundles can be scheduled (daily/weekly) or triggered on-demand and are written to tenant-configured residency-compliant storage endpoints (S3 region or on-prem path).
Retention-preview shows projected storage, expected sample count, and a downloadable CSV of example request ids that would be retained for the selected policy.
Runtime enforces deletion windows and sampling semantics within 24 hours of policy change; deletion logs are queryable by tenant and retained per retention policy for evidence.
Automated test suite covers sampling determinism, export integrity verification (checksum + signature), and cross-region residency mapping.
Product docs and compliance playbook published with step-by-step evidence verification instructions and regulator-ready artifact examples.
technical_notes: Retention engine lives in control plane and emits retention directives to storage indexers; indexer maintains metadata mapping (tenant, route, model, residency, retention-tier).
Sampling implemented as deterministic 64-bit hash(bucket) of (tenant_id||route_id||request_id||global_seed) so exports are reproducible across rollouts.

Evidence bundle format: manifest.json (bundle_id, time_range, sample_rate, tenant_id, route_ids, residency_locations), objects/{request_id}.ndjson.gz, checksums.sha256, manifest.sig (ECDSA-P256), keyinfo.kms (encrypted symmetric key info).
KMS integration required for bundle key wrapping and optional HSM signing for enterprise customers with BYOK.
Metric rollups retention separated: raw metrics kept short (30d default), aggregated rollups (hour/day) can be configured independently (90d/365d).
Cross-region considerations: if tenant residency is 'EU', exports must land in EU storage endpoint; cross-region fallback allowed only with explicit tenant permission recorded in audit log.
Deletion: soft-delete tombstones retained for 7 days for rollback then permanently purged per tier; purge jobs include signed purge-report for evidence.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): API + deterministic sampling + export bundle schema enabled for internal tenants and 3 pilot customers. Monitor correctness and signature verification. (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Add admin UI controls and retention-preview; enable scheduling exports to S3 destinations for pilot tenants. (3 weeks)
Phase 2: Expand to broader GA with docs, compliance playbook, and enable KMS BYOK options for enterprise. (4 weeks)
Migration: existing per-route TTLs mapped to 'hot' tier; admins can annotate routes for sampling — provide migration tool that computes projected sample counts before applying.
Rollback: ability to disable sampling and re-run bulk export for last-N days for compliance if sampling was misconfigured; audit trail required.
updates: 2025-11-10: Scoping workshop with Eng (Rohit S.), Security (Lena M.), and Solutions (Diego R.). Agreed on deterministic sampling approach and ECDSA for bundle signatures.
2025-12-02: Prototype of export bundle schema completed by Eng-RT; initial KMS keywrap integration validated in dev. See GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/inference-retention/pull/89.
2026-01-15: UX mockups reviewed. Design feedback: show example retained request ids and allow time-range slider in preview. Design ticket DES-612 created for UI polish.
2026-02-05: Pilot customer A (fintech) accepted canary export artifacts; requested stronger retention audit CSV with masked PII — added to scope as optional transform during export.
2026-02-28: Security review kickoff scheduled; draft threat model submitted. Noted concern: key escrow patterns for cross-region exports — Security to provide guidelines.
